Comments: On July 28, 2021, I conducted an inspection of the Papa Bear Well Site in Somerset Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of fluid reported to the Department on 7/28/2021. The initial report indicated that approximately 40 gallons of production fluid was released from a dump line associated with the Gas Production unit. At the time of inspection, EQT Rep. David Crayne, Jona Stoskey (Moody) and SPSI were on site evaluating the area impacted by the release. The release occurred from the dump line associated with GPU 10H well at a connection on the left side of the GPU. The area impacted by this release was previously impacted by a release of production fluid reported to the Department on 6/25/2021 IR 3212309 which occurred on the right side of the same 10H GPU. According to Ms. Stoskey, she was on site to collect confirmatory sample from the location in accordance with the Act 2 clean up when the release was observed and reported. Mr. Crayne indicated that the most recent spill would also be remediated in accordance with Act 2 and included with the release and clean up form the release on 6/25/2021. New violations area being issued based on the observations made during the site inspection. Violations remain outstanding as indicated on IR 321309.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-02-14 to Dorso Lp in New Stanton Boro, Westmoreland county. 102.4(b)4 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person failed to plan and implement earth disturbance activities to minimize duration & extent of earth disturbance, minimize soil compaction, maximize protection of drainage features and vegetation, and utilize other measures or controls that prevent or minimize the generation of increased stormwater runoff.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Dorso Lp
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-02-14
Violation Code: 102.4(b)4 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person failed to plan and implement earth disturbance activities to minimize duration & extent of earth disturbance, minimize soil compaction, maximize protection of drainage features and vegetation, and utilize other measures or controls that prevent or minimize the generation of increased stormwater runoff.
Violation ID: 877200
Permit API: 129-26159
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: New Stanton Boro
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 2020-02-14
Comments: This inspection is being conducted in response to a notification received by the Department from the operator of plugging being conducted at this site. Assisting with this inspection is WQS Eric Norman. Conditions on site are cloudy, light snow on the ground, and approximately 30 degrees. The access road appears rutted with several locations that have standing water present. One such location (Photo 1-3) has what appears to be an outfall basin where two streams meet and then pass under the access road via a culvert heading in the direction of Trib 37653 of Sewickley Creek. It appears that at this location some sediment laden water may have left the road in the vicinity of the hay bales (Photo 1), went down slope and discharged into this basin. At the time of this inspection it does not appear to be currently ongoing. The straw bale barriers at this location do not appear to have been installed correctly (See Standard Detail 4-13 in the E&S Manual 363-2134-008, pg. 90). The bales do not appear to have been staked, trenched, or back fill applied. This appears to have allowed sediment laden stormwater to go around the bales and enter WOTC. The Department recommends that the operator immediately address this deficiency in order to prevent any further impacts to WOTC. A second location (Photo's 4-7) is actively discharging sediment laden water into WOTC. The water appears to be pooling at a low point on the access road, spilling into a ditch which is conveying through a culvert pipe underneath the access road into a stream heading in the direction of Trib 37653 of Sewickley Creek. A straw bale barrier at this location does not appear to have been installed correctly (See Standard Detail 4-13 in the E&S Manual 363-2134-008, pg. 90). The bales do not appear to have been staked, trenched, or back fill applied. This appears to have allowed sediment laden stormwater to go around the bales and enter WOTC. The Department recommends that the operator immediately address this deficiency in order to prevent any further impacts to WOTC. The well appears plugged with a monument present with the API number affixed. There is no machinery present on the site. The site does not appear to have been temporarily stabilized and no down slope E&S controls are present. There does not appear to be an E&S Plan on site. The Department recommends that the operator take immediate steps to temporarily stabilize the site to prevent the potential for accelerated erosion or sedimentation. The Department recommends that the operator have E&S Plans prepared by a person trained and experienced in E&S Control methods and techniques applicable to the size and scope of the project and that those plans be on site during all phases of the earth disturbance activity. The Department also recommends that the operator installs downslope controls to prevent accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring at the site. An operator representative was spoken to via phone about the conditions on site. Mr. Wagner stated that no E&S Plans had been developed for this project and due to the weather conditions, no efforts were made to stabilize the site against accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Based on this inspection violations are being issued to the operator. The Department requests a timeline and action plan for abating the discharge and possible discharges identified in this inspection. Further violations may be issued based on responses received from the operator.

It appears that conditions of the direct portion of the access road leading to the Armstrong 2 gas well site are unchanged from IR 3891447, therefore violations issued for an inadequately stabilized shared and direct access road are to remain outstanding at this time. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the sediment that was piled along the edge of the access road near a hillside above a stream to be removed. Silt fencing was observed to be installed on site in this area and further downslope on this hillside right above a stream. The Department recommends the Operator ensure the fence stays trenched and taut in accordance with specifications. The clumps of sediment that the Department previously observed within the floodway and streambank of the stream adjacent to the shared access road was observed to be removed from the stream at the time of this inspection.Based on today's inspection, violations issued for sediment entering the WOC and for failure to implement E and S controls are being closed at this time, however, violations issued for an inadequately stabilized shared and direct access road are to remain outstanding at this time.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78a54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth and in accordance with 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
Violation ID: 8236447
Permit API: 125-24824
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Morris Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/03/2025
Comments: Inspection 2 of 2On 06/03/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the NV55HS Well Site following receipt of a spill report. The spill was reported to the Department on 06/02/2025 at 10:58am (CTS 389543). I was accompanied by Bruce Carpenter of CNX. Additional CNX representatives and SPSI were on site. The spill was reported to have occurred on 06/02/2025 at 7:30am. It was reported that produced water sprayed under the pad from one of the valves on the GPU. The release was contained and an unknown quantity was reported. No waterways were affected. The following was observed:Behind the GPU, a seep is present. Flow from this seep has allowed water to pool on the pad. This area was actively being vacuumed to remove any production fluid within the area. Absorbent materials were in use on site (Photos 1-3).Conductivity readings in the pooled area on the pad ranged from 375 uS/cm - 9.94 mS/cm (Photos 4-9).The water leads to a collection box on the pad, that outlets downslope of the pad. The shut off valve had been closed after the spill. No elevated conductivity was noted at the outlet off pad (Photos 10, 11).The operator updated the Department on 06/05/2025 that spill remediation has been completed. The Department requests an updated estimation of amount of fluid spilled. The Department also requests that a waste manifest be submitted as soon as possible. Due to the current estimated amount of fluid released being 4-5 gallons but threatening pollution to the Waters of the Commonwealth, and reporting the spill later than 2 hours after discovery, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) are being issued.

Comments: Site of oil release reported on 6/21/2019 was from the secondary containment of a tank battery located east off Salmon Road in a forested area. Oil was released from a hole in the bottom of one of the tanks located in a plastic lined secondary containment. An estimated several barrels of oil were released into the secondary containment. All contaminated soil was removed from the site and the clean up area was top soiled and stabilized with seed and mulch. All disturbed area restored with a good growth of vegetation growing in October until cold weather. A ditch was cut west through the field from the culvert discharge with no E&S controls which has resulted in erosion of the ditch. There are no E&S controls installed any where on this site. Water flowing from the culvert and upper areas of the restored areas are concentrating into a flow which has resulted in erosion and sedimentation on the north section of the restored area and off site as well. There are several erosion rills formed with the resulting sedimentation, E&S controls need to be installed immediately. Violations for erosion and sedimentation will be issued if controls are not installed. The report for the clean-up and restoration of the area needs to be submitted to the Department and approved before violations can be lifted.

Comments: This is a complaint inspection following a report by the operator of a large production water spill at this site on 4/26 at 7:30 am. An initial site visit was performed by WQSS Rob Bechtel. This inspection was performed with Seneca's Jeff Passerello.The initial spill occurred when a cast iron gate valve failed as the operator was pumping production water to a stimulation operation on the E09-U pad. The pump was in operation at 50 barrels per minute. The operator was able to stop the leak eventually. Water spread out across the northern edge of the site, entering a perimeter ditch. It then ran around the edge ditch of the site and eventually entered an infiltration berm on the southwest corner of the location. The operator brought in a pump and was able to collect a significant amount of liquid from this location. The operator's estimate is that 1500+ barrels of produced water was released. The operator has scraped up ~150 tons of material from the surface of the location and staged it on site to remove to the landfill. A pump is placed and the operator is using it to pump water collecting in the berm into tanks on site. Water does not appear to have passed the berm at this time, at least superficially. The operator has brought in ARM Group to do an initial analysis of the site and to take samples for removal to the landfill. Further inspection on this site will be done as necessary as cleanup continues.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/16/2025
Comments: On July 16, 2025 DEP conducted an Incident Inspection of EQT's Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County. EQT acquired the Porter Well Pad from Olympus on 7/1/2025 (Transfer approved by the DEP on 7/14/2025), therefore EQT takes full responsibility of the incident addressed in IR 4004278, where violations were issued for a 1-3 barrel release of a produced water, freshwater and frack chemical mixture. Accompanying during today's inspection was EQT's Lance Barnes, Olympus's Kyle Borden and SPSI's Joe Perry.At the time of this inspection an Act 9 sign was observed at the access road entrance and in the on-site mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan. Operator information on the sign does not match the plans. The DEP recommends the Operator promptly update the plans as applicable. An access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed.During IR 4004278, the DEP screened the release area and collected elevated conductivity readings in an area that was scraped 2-4 inches deep as well as at the base/underneath an AST (inadvertently referred to as freshwater impoundment in IR 4004278) on site. At the time of that inspection, Olympus's Laura Karosic stated once fracking is complete (7/11-12/ 2024), the AST would be removed from the well site and further remediation efforts would be conducted in the release area.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the AST to be removed from the well site. The area where the AST was as well as the previously scraped release area all appeared to be newly scraped. A ditch was observed to be dug and bordering the secondary containment within the release area. The DEP utilized a conductivity meter to screen the newly scraped release area as well as the ditch. The DEP collected soil readings of 0.0171 mS, 0.0605 mS, and 0.026 mS in the newly scraped release area, and 2.33 mS in a puddle of cloudy fluid observed in the ditch. These conductivity readings were compared to a background soil reading taken on the well site perimeter (0.1247 mS). The readings collected in the scraped areas are comparable to the background reading, however readings collected in the ditch are elevated. At the time of this inspection, Mr. Barnes and Mr. Perry informed the DEP that the observed to be newly scraped release area is reportedly remediated, however the ditch and area underneath the containment is not. The DEP inquired why/how the area under the containment is contaminated when the release originated on top of the containment. Mr. Perry hypothesized that released fluids that were sitting on the graveled well pad/under the AST were washed underneath the secondary containment during heavy rainfall following the release. Once the rain ceased and the AST was removed, contaminated fluids leached out from under the containment in the release area, therefore the ditch is being utilized to catch and contain any of the leached contaminated fluid. Mr. Barnes and Mr. Borden stated that drilling will be completed in approx. 8-10 days, then the containment will be pulled and remediation efforts will be conducted in the remaining contaminated locations.The DEP recommends the EQT promptly remediate the release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(2).During IR 4004278 the DEP requested the following:-The Operator submit a written response that includes an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations and how the Operator quantified the amount released.-The Operator follow Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) -The Operator assess the impacts to the WOC from the release.-The Operator submit a NOV response by 7/23/25.--These have yet to be received as of 7/16/25Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued to EQT for the 1-3 barrel release and for failure to remove the contaminated fluid from the ground within 15 days of the pollution incident.

Comments: On 4/21/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 52 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the active north pad, I met with Seneca's Adam Pierce who described current operations as follows: Evolution Well Services has been on site since 2/13/2026, performing stimulation operations on eight recently drilled gas wells. The crew was currently alternating between the 70HU, 204HU, 203HU, and 72HU. The crew has completed conducting stimulation stages on the other four wells. Adam expects stimulation activities on the eight wells to be completed by 6/8/2026.In addition to 28 frac tanks that were stationed on the west side of the pad during previous operations, four freshwater frac tanks, four pump down frac tanks, two gas buster frac tanks and five working frac tanks have been staged on the pad. These tanks are staged in secondary containment.Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs that are connected to the completed wells are stationed in secondary containment.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. During the inspection, I screened liquid in a 3' x 1.5' x 5" deep puddle, above the center outfall on the north side of the pad, the result being 9.40 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-242 from the puddle.I screened liquid flowing into the southeast corner of the sediment basin from the rock lined outfall from the pad, the result being 10.30 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-243 from the flowing liquid.I screened liquid in the sediment pond next to the east overflow, the result being 3.04 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-244 from the pond.I screened liquid flowing north from the sediment basin, past the last compost filter sock and past the LOD, the result being 3.33 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-245 from the flowing liquid.The original south pad and access road for the Taft 851 1V well have been returned to original grade with vegetation becoming effective. Separate construction projects are underway, installing water and gas pipelines on the south side of the pad.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1545 hours.

Inspection Date: 1/10/2022
Comments: On January 10, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Pad in response to a spill notification received on January 10, 2022. DEP spoke with Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources. Mr. Rodriguez said that a hose that manifolded multiple frac tanks onsite broke and released approximately 1,600 barrels of production fluid water from frac tanks. There were 17 frac tanks onsite in secondary containment for flow back storage from recent stimulation of the wells on the pad. The secondary containment of the frac tanks was overwhelmed and some of the production fluid water spilled to the pad surface. The amount of production fluid that was spilled to the pad surface is still being calculated. The spill was first noticed on January 8, 2022 but STL Resources failed to notify the DEP emergency spill line. The production fluid ran into a drain on the southwest corner of the well pad which outlets off the pad into a infiltration berm. An area 60 yds. x 40 yds. of the pad surface was impacted by production fluid. Off the pad area of impact was about 20 ft. wide by 120 ft. long. At the time of inspection, STL Resources contractors were vacuuming up the free standing production fluid out of the drainage outlet and the fluid pooled up in front of the infiltration berm. The DEP measured soil conductivity around the area of impact on the well pad and multiple measurements resulted in over range readings of the soil conductivity meter. Soil conductivity off the pad surface where the production fluid water flowed into the infiltration berm also resulted in an over range readings. The maximum conductivity measurement of the soil conductivity meter is 4,000 microsiemens per centimeter. STL Resources have contractors scheduled to arrive today to delineate the area of impact and to remove the impacted soils. Violations of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), Chapter 78a.66(b)2, Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. The DEP recommends STL Resources begin the Act 2 process.

Violation ID: 8233562
Permit API: 031-23676
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Monroe Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/15/2025
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an ongoing investigation into stray gas migration, involving combustible gas detected at the foundation of a nearby private residence. The well is situated approximately 650 feet north-northwest of the complainant’s residence. During the inspection, an updated well record was reviewed. The well was actively producing via the 4-inch production string, with valves on the 7-inch intermediate casing and the 4-inch production string annuls closed at the time of inspection Bubbling was observed in the annular space between the 9-5/8-inch surface casing and the 7-inch intermediate casing. Combustible gas screening using a calibrated gas meter indicated a concentration of 29% LEL (1.4%) in this annulus. According to the well records, both the 9-5/8-inch surface casing and the 7-inch intermediate casing were cemented to surface. The presence of combustible gas in the annulus suggests potential defects in the casing and/or cement integrity. Additionally, no check valve was observed on the production lines exiting the well. To further assess possible migration, four slam bar holes were installed approximately 6 inches to 1 foot from the wellhead in the cardinal directions, each about 3 feet deep. No detectable levels of combustible gas were found in the slam bar holes at the time of the inspection. A Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II meter, calibrated on 05/15/2025 was used for combustible gas screening during the inspection. It is noted that the operator has not responded to or completed the recommended corrective actions outlined in Inspection ID# 3913271. These actions were communicated via certified mail (USPS# 9589 0710 5270 1975 0616 42), sent on 02/13/2025 and received by the operator on 02/19/2025. As a result, the violations identified during this inspection are now being formally imposed on this well.

Permit API: 063-34032
Unconventional: No

Comments: On 6/2/22 at 0900 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Turm Oil, Inc.'s Paul Strong 4 well (API 063-34032) in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. Mr. Bill Davis with Turm Oil was also present during the inspection. The inspection was conducted in response to a complaint, received by the Department on 6/1/22, of oil and produced water being released from a production fluids tank that was being removed from the site.I spoke with the complainant, the operator, and Mr. Davis on 6/1/22. The operator informed me that the well was sold to Rosebud Mining back in March; however there is no record of a well transfer filed with the Department. During our phone call, Mr. Davis informed me that the tank removal and release occurred around 1100 hrs. on 5/31/22. He estimated that approximately 10 gallons of crude oil and production fluid was released when removing the tank, and stated that some absorbent material was placed near the well and was subsequently containerized. Mr. Davis also acknowledged that some released fluid was covered up during regrading of the site.Upon inspection of the site, oil stained soil and vegetation was observed, beginning at the regraded area of the well pad, and continuing along a drainage ditch adjacent to the pad. There was a strong crude oil odor present. The impacted water in the ditch flowed to a nearby ephemeral stream where a slight sheen was observed. The black plastic bag containing the absorbent material Mr. Davis previously applied was located at the base of the well head; however, no additional measures were taken to prevent the material from reaching Waters of the Commonwealth. I advised Mr. Davis to place absorbent boom or pads to prevent further downstream impacts. I also advised Mr. Davis that regulations require removal of the pollutant from the soil and water within 15 days. In addition, I requested that Mr. Davis reinstall a well tag with the permit number on the well head.The release was not reported to the Department. Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), 91.34(A), 78.66(b), and78.66(e) are cited and will be immediately closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), CSL 402(b), 78.54, 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(a), and SWMA 610(1) are being cited for the release of crude oil and production fluid onto the ground and into Waters of the Commonwealth. These violations will be resolved upon remediation and temporary stabilization of the site, and submission of waste manifests for the disposal of impacted material to the Department.

Permit API: 121-44938
Unconventional: No
County: Venango
Municipality: Pinegrove Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-09-10
Comments: Onsite for a spill response that was reported by the operator. The release occurred near the Hart 3 well. It is believed that there was a failure in a fitting along the pipeline that allowed the leak to occur, but was not excavated yet. The operator has hired a clean-up contractor (ECS&R)) who was onsite investigating the extent of the release and removing crude oil from the watercourse. The crude oil pushed to the surface at the Hart 3 well and there is oil that has traveled over the ground near the well. It also appears oil has traveled subsurface possibly in a trench for the electric. There is oil seeping out underneath a culvert approximately 100 feet north west. The oil continues to follow the watercourse in a northwest direction for approximately another 200 feet. The contractors are setting up defensive measures to prevent oil from entering a pond that is fed by the watercourse. The pond is located approximately 50 feet past the last visible oil. Contractor intends to remain onsite removing oil from the watercourse and continue in investigate the extent of the release. Violations are noted.

Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.

Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Wetmore Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/26/2024
Comments: This conventional well is equipped for production with a pump jack. A sign containing the API number, well name, and operator information was posted on a stake near the well. This inspection was conducted in response to a phone call from JR McLaughlin, a representative from Bull Run Resources, reporting a minor leak which had occurred at Well M22. Upon arrival to the site, it was evident that crude oil had recently leaked from a faulty line near the well head. The discharged crude oil remained on the well site. It is estimated that less than 1 barrel of crude oil has been released as part of this incident. No waterways have been affected from the event.The broken line had already been repaired before arriving to the site. Several workers from Bull Run Resources were actively shoveling contaminated soil and snow to be removed from the site. An excavator had been used to scrape the ground surface where the crude oil had discharged. The excavated area was seeded and mulched upon arrival to the site. Given there is no ongoing discharge and the impacted area appears to have been sufficiently remediated, the violations associated with this incident are considered corrected. A future inspection will be conducted to ensure that the initial remediation efforts were sufficient.

Permit API: 051-21986
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Redstone Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/19/2026
Comments: On March 19, 2026, the DEP conducted a Follow Up Inspection in response to IRs 4157087, 4157136, 4157162, 4157480, and 4157532. This inspection is separated into 2 inspection reports and discusses 8 observed culverts along the access road as well as any observed erosion and sedimentation issues along the access road. This Inspection Report is Inspection 1 of 2 and assesses Culverts 1-5. All associated violations discussed in both inspection reports are being issued/continued in just this inspection.A COA with the DEP was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, a rig was on site and plugging operations have commenced.During IRs 4157087/4157136/4157162, the DEP recommended the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan and redline the site plans to appropriately match on-site field changes.During IRs 4157480/4157532, the DEP recommended the operator install CFS along the access road in all sections of E and S off of the access road and above each culvert inlet and outlet, as well as gravel the access road at all culvert crossings in accordance with the E and S plan. The DEP recommended the operator install orange construction fence along the access road near the seep and wetland identified near the culvert 4 inlet and past culvert 5. The DEP recommended the operator restore the roadside ditch at seep.At the time of this inspection, the E and S plan was present in the on-site mailbox at the beginning of the access road. The DEP did not observed any redlining on site plans to depict and appropriately match on-site field changes (Photo 2). The DEP also did not observe the RCE to be installed at the beginning of the access road as depicted on the plans (Photo 1). The access road was also observed to still not be graveled by the operator despite the E and S plan calling for the road to be "graveled as necessary". CFS was observed to be installed at an area where erosion and sedimentation off the access road was previously noted to be located before culvert 1.Observations obtained during today's inspection at culvert crossings 1-5 are as follows:Culvert 1 crossing - culverted for a roadside ditch (Photos 4-7): The outlet still appears to be block. CFS was observed at both the inlet and outlet, however, the CFS at the outlet is improperly installed as complete surface contact to the ground was not observed. Culvert 2 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 8-9): Outlet still appears to be blocked. CFS was observed to be installed and functioning properly at both the inlet and outlet. Culvert 3 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 10-13): The inlet to this culvert appears to still be blocked. CFS was installed at both the inlet and outlet of this culvert, however, the CFS at the inlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. No sediment was observed to be entering the stream at this time.Culvert 4 crossing - culverted for roadside ditch (Photos 14-17): CFS was observed to be installed at both the inlet and outlet of this culvert, however, the CFS at the inlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. Culvert still appears to not be receiving water due to operator disturbing channel and causing water to be diverted further down access road. The disturbed channel still appears to be carrying fine sediment towards the stream at culvert 5, however no sediment was observed entering the stream due to the second half of the channel going subsurface with the entry point into the stream unseen (Photos 18-20).Culvert 5 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 21-24): CFS was observed to be installed at both the inlet and outlet of this crossing, however, the CFS at the outlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. No sediment was observed to be entering the stream at this time.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/18/2024
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8202007
Permit API: 129-26861
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Derry Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/18/2024
Comments: On September 18, 2024 the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Diversified's Davenport Well Site located in Derry Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3774486 where violations were issued for an 18-20 barrel release of production fluid from a production tank on June 4, 2024.At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared stabilized with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed and the production tank that was leaking during IR 3774486 has since been removed from the well site. A well tag was fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it, and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges was observed coming from or near the wellhead. The area where the production tank once (where the spill originated), the slope that the spill traveled down, and the area downstream where the spill pooled up at now appears to be backfilled, seeded and mulched pending vegetative growth. In addition, at the edge of the downslope area right before a forested area began, some black fencing was observed.Several soil conductivity readings were taken in the spill areas (0.0418 mS, 0.0362 mS, 0.0054 mS, 0.0137 mS, and 0.0602 mS) and are significantly lower than the soil conductivity readings taken in the same areas at the time of the spill (Soil conductivity readings taken on 6/4/24 documented in IR 3774486: 1.35 mS, 1.454 mS, Over Range, 7.63 mS, 5.51 mS, and 4.90 mS). Upon inspection of the fence, two areas appeared to be compromised. A stake appeared to be snapped and the fence appeared to be pushed down by sediment, at this time, there did not appear to be any evidence of the sediment overtopping the fence and no erosion or sedimentation was observed behind this section of fence. Another section of the fence right behind a small tree appeared to not be trenched and a gap was observed between the bottom of the fence and the ground. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed behind this section of the fence a this time either.The Department is recommending the Operator promptly properly implement and maintain the temporary erosion and sedimentation (E and S) best management practices (BMPs) to prevent any pollution from occurring.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to properly implement and maintain E and S BMPs. In addition, violations issued during IR 3774486 shall remain outstanding until the Act 2 Report is submitted, received, reviewed and approved by the Environmental Cleanup and Brownfields (ECB) Program.
